Performers
London Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Pierre Monteux (conductor) Documented

Both the Internet Archive description and the Decca booklet credit the London Symphony Orchestra under Monteux. The leader and principals on this session are not documented here; the booklet’s essay says that Hugh Maguire joined as leader after the orchestra’s 1957 arrival of young players, without tying that to this date.

[1] [2]
Work version
The 1903 final version, as published by Fazer & Westerlund (the version in general use); the performing edition of this recording has not been checked against a score Inferred, not documented

The Sibelius Society gives the first version (premiere 8 March 1902) and the final version of 1903. The 1958 recording would normally use the published score; the Decca booklet lists Breitkopf & Härtel as publisher of the edition. No source states which version Monteux used, and no score alignment was made.

[4] [3]
Recorded
18–⁠20 June 1958 Documented

The Decca booklet gives Kingsway Hall, 18–⁠20 June 1958, for the disc whose track list holds this symphony (PDF page 21, printed p. 40, beside the track list on PDF page 20, printed p. 39; the 24 and 25 June 1958 sessions marked with an asterisk are for Elgar’s Enigma Variations on the same disc). The Internet Archive description narrows the date to 20 June 1958 without a source. The identification rests on the layout of the booklet’s credits, which the author read as attaching to the disc listing Sibelius and Elgar; the measured movement lengths of this file (10:17, 14:36, 6:14 and 12:49) match the booklet’s track times (10:16, 14:36, 6:15, 12:49).

[2] [1]
Place
Kingsway Hall, London Documented

Both sources name Kingsway Hall.

[2] [1]
Label
RCA (US catalogue LSC 2342; UK catalogue SB 207); Decca reissue SDD 234 (September 1970) Documented

The booklet’s “First released as” line names the catalogue numbers and months but not the label name for SB 207. The Internet Archive description says Decca–RCA. The author treats the first issue as RCA’s.

[2]
Catalogue
RCA LSC 2342 (October 1959); SB 207 (May 1960); Decca SDD 234 (September 1970) Documented

The first issue was in October 1959 (LSC 2342) and May 1960 (SB 207); both dates are before 1963.

[2]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

The booklet names no matrix, take or side numbers.

[2]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The Internet Archive item was uploaded by a private account (subject tag “DWTKenInNY”); its description names no transfer engineer or source disc.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item’s public date is 11 June 2023; that is an upload date, not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
A single VBR MP3 of the whole symphony; the uploader’s movement times are given in the description Documented

The Internet Archive derivative is a 78.7 MB VBR MP3 lasting 2,637 seconds. Whether it was sourced from an LP, CD or tape is not stated. No further processing is disclosed.

[1]
Composition rights
Sibelius died in 1957, so the symphony (published 1903) is in copyright in countries with a life-plus-70 term, including the EU, until the end of 2027; IMSLP records it as public domain in the United States, Canada and life-plus-50 countries Documented

The IMSLP work page carries a notice that the work is not in the public domain in life-plus-70 countries. The end date of 2027 is computed from Sibelius’s death in 1957, which the site’s Sibelius biography gives as 20 September 1957. This dossier does not claim the composition is out of copyright in the EU. The programme’s rule applies to the sound recording, not the composition.

[3]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — EU public domain (territorial): first published before 1963 (RCA LSC 2342, October 1959; SB 207, May 1960). Documented

Territorial only: the recording’s first publication in 1959–⁠60 predates 1963, so its EU 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. The United States status of a 1958–⁠59 sound recording is not established here. The Internet Archive item carries no licence URL; its metadata and description contain no non-commercial restriction. The item belongs to a general “folksoundomy” collection and was uploaded by a third party, not by the rights holder.

[2] [1]

Jean Sibelius, Symphony No. 2 in D major, Op. 43. London Symphony Orchestra, Pierre Monteux, conductor. Recorded at Kingsway Hall, London, 18–⁠20 June 1958; first issued as RCA LSC 2342 (1959). Single-file Internet Archive upload, item sibelius-2-compl-monteux-lso. Territorial public-domain basis (first published before 1963). Rights statement
